Royal Heights is an MLS® area in northwest Surrey, around Royal Heights Park near 96 Avenue and Scott Road (120 Street). Between 96 and 102 Avenue it meets Cedar Hills along Scott Road. The park was set up in the mid-1960s, when the streets around it were first built.

Written by Jared Gibbons, REALTOR®, Royal LePage Little Oak Realty, on October 13, 2026. I have worked in Fraser Valley real estate since 2015. Rules and boundaries change, so confirm anything important with the City of Surrey and Surrey Schools.
Not legal, planning or financial advice. Confirm zoning, plan designations and school catchments before you buy or sell.

blocks.text: What to look at in a Royal Heights home

parts.t: These are the questions I go through with buyers.
Lot size, the age of the roof, furnace, plumbing and wiring, and drainage
What the zone allows, and whether any suite was built with a permit
Assuming you can add a suite or rebuild just because a neighbour did
Strata fees, the depreciation report (the plan for future repairs), meeting minutes and bylaws
About upcoming special levies (extra one-time charges) and what the fees include

items.t: Pet, rental or age rules that don’t fit your plans

parts.t: Zoning and plan designations can be different for each lot.

Around Royal Heights Park, a group of 127 lots had its own zone that limited house size and height. Council endorsed a City-led rezoning of the Royal Heights Park neighbourhood from that zone (CD) to R3, so confirm a lot's zone in COSMOS.
The City says most homes in that group of lots were built from the late 1950s to the early 1970s.
